content.text:
Every shell command after the initial listing was auto-denied, so I can't run further checks. The remaining work is the summary.

`0.svg` is now a complete, well-formed SVG that draws the numeral zero. One caveat first: I could not verify it with tools. This session has no way to approve shell permissions, so the XML check and the PNG render were both blocked before they ran. I checked the markup by hand instead. It is small enough that I'm confident it is valid and draws correctly.

**What was wrong.** The original file was a single empty element with nothing inside it:

```xml
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"/>
```

It had no viewBox, no size, no content, and no accessible name. In a browser it rendered as a blank box at the default size.

**What the new file has:**
- A viewBox plus an intrinsic size of 64 by 64, so it scales cleanly and sizes correctly in an img tag.
- A title and description wired up with role img, so screen readers announce it as "Zero". The ids are prefixed to avoid collisions when several SVGs are inlined on one page.
- The numeral drawn as a stroked ellipse, with margins chosen so the stroke never clips at the edges.
- A stroke of `currentColor`, which renders black on its own and follows the surrounding CSS color when inlined in HTML.

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
     viewBox="0 0 64 64"
     width="64" height="64"
     role="img"
     aria-labelledby="zero-title zero-desc">
  <title id="zero-title">Zero</title>
  <desc id="zero-desc">The numeral 0, drawn as a single outlined oval.</desc>
  <ellipse cx="32" cy="32" rx="15" ry="23"
           fill="none"
           stroke="currentColor"
           stroke-width="6"/>
</svg>
```

**Assumption.** The file had no content, so the name was the only hint about what it should show. I drew a zero on that basis. If the file was meant to hold a different graphic, the ellipse is the only line that needs replacing.

**To verify it yourself**, open the file in a browser or select it in Finder and press space. For a strict syntax check:

```
xmllint --noout /private/tmp/gndfv/0.svg
```
